python - <<'PY'
import json, os, math
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
from matplotlib import patheffects as pe

base=Path('/app')
with open(base/'benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data=json.load(f)['national_development']
rows=data['data']
df=pd.DataFrame(rows)

metrics=[
    ('gdp_per_capita_usd','GDP per capita\n(USD, log scale)'),
    ('hdi','HDI\n(index)'),
    ('freedom_index','Freedom\n(score 0–100)'),
    ('corruption_perceptions_index','CPI\n(score 0–100)'),
    ('co2_emissions_per_capita_tons','CO₂ emissions\n(t/person)'),
    ('military_expenditure_pct_gdp','Military spend\n(% of GDP)'),
    ('internet_penetration_pct','Internet use\n(% population)'),
]

# Transform GDP logarithmically for legibility while keeping labels in original units.
transformed={}
mins={}; maxs={}
for col,label in metrics:
    vals=df[col].astype(float).to_numpy()
    if col=='gdp_per_capita_usd':
        vals_t=np.log10(vals)
    else:
        vals_t=vals
    transformed[col]=vals_t
    mins[col]=float(np.nanmin(vals_t)); maxs[col]=float(np.nanmax(vals_t))

# Normalize each dimension to [0,1], preserving high=top for all dimensions.
norm=pd.DataFrame(index=df.index)
for col,_ in metrics:
    span=maxs[col]-mins[col]
    norm[col]=(transformed[col]-mins[col])/span if span else 0.5

# Group statistics for subtle background bands.
group_order=['High','Upper-Middle','Lower-Middle','Low']
colors={
    'High':'#1f77b4',          # policy/report blue
    'Upper-Middle':'#2ca02c',  # green
    'Lower-Middle':'#ff7f0e',  # amber
    'Low':'#8c564b',           # brown
}
light_colors={
    'High':'#dbeaf7',
    'Upper-Middle':'#e1f0df',
    'Lower-Middle':'#fff0dc',
    'Low':'#efe4df',
}

x=np.arange(len(metrics))
fig=plt.figure(figsize=(18,10.5), dpi=180)
ax=fig.add_axes([0.055,0.125,0.74,0.735])
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#fbfbf7')
ax.set_facecolor('#fbfbf7')

# Draw inter-axis income group envelopes to emphasize separation/overlap.
for group in group_order[::-1]:
    sub=norm[df['income_group']==group]
    low=sub[[c for c,_ in metrics]].quantile(0.20).to_numpy()
    high=sub[[c for c,_ in metrics]].quantile(0.80).to_numpy()
    for i in range(len(metrics)-1):
        poly_x=[x[i],x[i+1],x[i+1],x[i]]
        poly_y=[low[i],low[i+1],high[i+1],high[i]]
        ax.fill(poly_x, poly_y, color=light_colors[group], alpha=0.22, linewidth=0, zorder=0)

# Gridlines and axes.
for i,(col,label) in enumerate(metrics):
    ax.vlines(i, 0, 1, color='#3f3f3f', lw=1.2, zorder=2)
    for yy in np.linspace(0,1,6):
        ax.hlines(yy, i-0.045, i+0.045, color='#555555', lw=0.75, zorder=2)
for yy in np.linspace(0,1,6):
    ax.hlines(yy, -0.03, len(metrics)-0.97, color='#d8d8d0', lw=0.55, zorder=0, alpha=0.55)

# Determine outliers based on within-group robust z scores and mentioned profiles.
outlier_names=set()
for group in group_order:
    idx=df.index[df['income_group']==group]
    sub=norm.loc[idx,[c for c,_ in metrics]]
    med=sub.median()
    mad=(sub-med).abs().median().replace(0, np.nan)
    robust=((sub-med).abs()/mad).max(axis=1)
    for j,val in robust.nlargest(2).items():
        if val>=2.2:
            outlier_names.add(df.loc[j,'country'])
# Explicit data-driven profile deviations aligned to goal.
for _,r in df.iterrows():
    if r['income_group']=='High' and r['co2_emissions_per_capita_tons']>=14:
        outlier_names.add(r['country'])
    if r['income_group']=='Upper-Middle' and r['freedom_index']<=25:
        outlier_names.add(r['country'])

# Plot all polylines; highlighted outliers get stronger strokes.
for _,r in df.iterrows():
    group=r['income_group']
    ys=[norm.loc[r.name,col] for col,_ in metrics]
    is_out=r['country'] in outlier_names
    lw=2.6 if is_out else 1.35
    alpha=0.88 if is_out else 0.42
    z=5 if is_out else 3
    line=ax.plot(x, ys, color=colors[group], lw=lw, alpha=alpha, zorder=z, solid_capstyle='round')[0]
    if is_out:
        line.set_path_effects([pe.Stroke(linewidth=lw+1.8, foreground='white', alpha=0.78), pe.Normal()])

# Labels for selected outliers, positioned to avoid severe crowding.
label_specs={
    'United Arab Emirates': ('CO₂ outlier', 4, 0.035),
    'Saudi Arabia': ('high military + low freedom', 5, -0.035),
    'Australia': ('high CO₂ among high-income', 4, -0.06),
    'China': ('upper-middle, low freedom', 2, 0.04),
    'Russia': ('military + freedom divergence', 5, 0.045),
    'Singapore': ('freedom–CPI split', 3, 0.055),
}
for name,(note,axis_idx,dy) in label_specs.items():
    if name in set(df['country']):
        rr=df[df['country']==name].iloc[0]
        y=norm.loc[rr.name, metrics[axis_idx][0]]
        ax.scatter([axis_idx],[y], s=28, color=colors[rr['income_group']], edgecolor='white', lw=0.9, zorder=7)
        tx=min(axis_idx+0.08, len(metrics)-1.04)
        ha='left'
        if axis_idx>=len(metrics)-2:
            tx=axis_idx-0.10; ha='right'
        ax.annotate(f"{name}\n{note}", xy=(axis_idx,y), xytext=(tx,y+dy), textcoords='data',
                    ha=ha, va='center', fontsize=8.1, color='#242424', zorder=8,
                    bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.25', fc='#fffdf7', ec='#cfcfc6', lw=0.65, alpha=0.92),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color='#777777', lw=0.7, shrinkA=2, shrinkB=2))

# Axis labels and tick labels based on original values.
for i,(col,label) in enumerate(metrics):
    ax.text(i, 1.085, label, ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10.2, weight='bold', color='#1f1f1f')
    if col=='gdp_per_capita_usd':
        ticks_orig=[1000,3000,10000,30000,100000]
        ticks=[]
        for val in ticks_orig:
            t=(math.log10(val)-mins[col])/(maxs[col]-mins[col])
            if -0.02<=t<=1.02:
                ticks.append((t, f'${val/1000:g}k'))
    elif col=='hdi':
        ticks_orig=[0.4,0.6,0.8,0.96]
        ticks=[((val-mins[col])/(maxs[col]-mins[col]), f'{val:.2f}') for val in ticks_orig]
    elif col=='co2_emissions_per_capita_tons':
        ticks_orig=[0,5,10,15,20]
        ticks=[((val-mins[col])/(maxs[col]-mins[col]), f'{val:g}') for val in ticks_orig if mins[col]-0.01<=val<=maxs[col]+0.01]
    elif col=='military_expenditure_pct_gdp':
        ticks_orig=[1,2,4,6]
        ticks=[((val-mins[col])/(maxs[col]-mins[col]), f'{val:g}%') for val in ticks_orig]
    else:
        ticks_orig=[20,40,60,80,100]
        ticks=[((val-mins[col])/(maxs[col]-mins[col]), f'{val:g}') for val in ticks_orig if mins[col]-0.01<=val<=maxs[col]+0.01]
    for yy,txt in ticks:
        if 0<=yy<=1:
            ax.text(i-0.062, yy, txt, ha='right', va='center', fontsize=7.6, color='#555555')

# Emphasize Freedom -> CPI cluster interval.
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((1.88,-0.035), 1.24, 1.07, facecolor='#ece7f2', edgecolor='#8e77a7', lw=0.9, alpha=0.18, zorder=1))
ax.text(2.5, -0.085, 'Freedom → CPI: clustering vs. divergence', ha='center', va='top', fontsize=9.2, color='#5c4a6b', weight='bold')

# Add crossover cue along the axis chain.
ax.annotate('Crossovers reveal nonlinear profiles\n(e.g., high income but low freedom, or high CO₂)',
            xy=(3.55,0.57), xytext=(4.25,1.12), fontsize=9.3, color='#333333',
            ha='left', va='center',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.32', fc='#fffdf7', ec='#cfcfc6', lw=0.7),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#555555', lw=0.9, connectionstyle='arc3,rad=-0.22'))

ax.set_xlim(-0.35,len(metrics)-0.65)
ax.set_ylim(-0.12,1.16)
ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

# Title/subtitle.
fig.text(0.055,0.955,'National Development Profiles Across Seven Indicators',
         ha='left', va='top', fontsize=20, weight='bold', color='#171717')
